bull_bear.body: - Net cash +INR 170 cr; debt-light (INR 72 cr total incl. leases, down from INR 140 cr). Expansion funded largely via internal accruals + IPO proceeds (INR 194 cr unutilised). Disciplined IRR/return-based allocation. Board-approved treasury policy parks surplus in liquid/overnight funds (~INR 700 cr rotation; other income ~INR 2 cr/qtr, INR 68 lakh in Q4). No dividend mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **APM gas allocation cuts** + rising ceiling/NWG prices → high-cost gas (mitigant: pass-through, HPHT, domestic sourcing, priority allocation).
- **Gas-sourcing/geopolitical:** Gulf war disrupted LNG; force-majeure invoked (restricted to industrial). Long-term contracts (Shell/GSPC, portfolio-based not Qatar-specific) provide insulation.
- **Industrial demand destruction** in Fatehgarh Sahib (DCQ cuts, higher prices, AAP-era de-growth); NGT order implementation deferred to avoid agitating customers.
- **EV/CNG price-competitiveness** (mainly Tamil Nadu); late-licensed high-capex GA economics take time to match incumbents (IGL/MGL).
- JV receivable recoverability (Ni Hon); execution risk on aggressive N&T rollout / new TN government policy.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and candid, but explicitly cautious on hard guidance given "evolving" geopolitical/sourcing situation ("giving a predictable guidance is a challenge... I hope my investors will pardon me"). Repeatedly stresses margin protection via pass-through and net-cash discipline. Proud of 150-station landmark and accident-free year. Transparent on Q4 one-offs and willingness to walk through P&L line items with investors.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- ~40% of CNG volume tied to NWG/APM; APM cut offset by NWG — sourcing mix is the real margin driver, not headline price.
- HPHT gas (IGX, prorated allocation) is the competitive swing source and got CHEAPER in Q4, a hidden tailwind.
- Late-licensed CGDs structurally disadvantaged on capex intensity & sourcing scale vs IGL/MGL, but win on private-sector operational efficiency.
- Shizuoka Gas (Japan shareholder) provides essentially no sourcing/technical benefit — min LNG ship size (~40,000 units) too large.
- Treasury earns meaningful float income via daily dealer-proceed collection by 1 pm parked in overnight funds.
- New labour code forced ~INR 60 lakh extra provisioning (industry-wide Q4 effect).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Net-debt-free positioning: "IRM enters FY27 on a net-debt-free balance sheet; provides headroom to fund infrastructure outlay without external leverage", with total debt (incl. long-term lease) falling from Rs.228.30 Cr (FY24) to Rs.139.57 Cr (FY25) to Rs.72.15 Cr (FY26) and debt-equity from 0.25x to 0.15x to 0.07x.
- Liquidity: at Q1FY27 the glance page shows total debt of Rs.49 cr, cash and bank balance of Rs.254 cr and net worth of Rs.1,033 cr as on 30 Jun 2026 (net worth footnoted as "Net Worth as on 31st March 2026 + Q1FY27 PAT"); the FY26 appendix separately shows total debt Rs.72.15 Cr, cash and bank Rs.242.55 Cr, investments Rs.33.94 Cr, total cash and bank Rs.276.49 Cr and "Available Surplus Funds" of Rs.170.40 Cr.
- Credit ratings carried on the glance page: "IND AA- Stable / IND A1+" and "CRISIL AA- Negative / CRISIL A1+" - note the differing outlooks between the two agencies.
- "During Q1FY27, the promoter group increased its stake by 0.67%, underscoring its confidence in the Company's long-term growth prospects."
- Capital-allocation philosophy is stated qualitatively as "Prudent capital allocation, network monetisation reduce execution risk while supporting sustainable growth"; no dividend policy or payout is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **CNG:** ~61% of total operational revenue; most profitable (margin & net-margin) segment; ~75-80% of CNG sourcing from domestic gas. New 3-wheeler sales ~92-95% CNG in Namakkal-Trichy; Banaskantha passenger-vehicle CNG penetration >40%, N&T >15% and rising. Spot purchases only ~4% of full-year CNG.
- **Industrial PNG:** concentrated in Fatehgarh Sahib (industrial zone); hit by DCQ cuts and demand destruction from higher prices; Banaskantha industrial +13% YoY; awaiting NGT order implementation to lift volumes off low base.
- **Domestic/commercial PNG:** strong adds; rising LPG-substitution demand (LPG shortage driving conversions in hotels/commercial); PNGRB mandate caps domestic coverage at ~1/3 of population.
business.title: Segment (CNG / industrial / domestic)

business.body:
- Regulated CGD model presented as the core moat: "Long-term PNGRB licenses across 4 GAs strong revenue visibility, predictable cash flows, and limited competitive intensity. Regulatory framework provides a strong moat and downside protection."
- Four PNGRB-authorised GAs covering six districts - Banaskantha (GJ), Fatehgarh Sahib (PB), Diu & Gir Somnath (GJ) and Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli (TN) - "Addressing total population of 1.2+ Cr across 4 GA's on annuity basis".
- Penetration runway framed on the transport side: "CNG Vehicles at 15% of 7.8 Lacs registered vehicles in 4 GAs"; per-GA CNG vehicle counts are Banaskantha 91,087, Diu & Gir Somnath 14,381, Namakkal & Tiruchirappalli 9,945 and Fatehgarh Sahib 1,898.
- Investment rationale slide lists six pillars: regulated CGD business with high visibility; structural demand growth from energy transition; volume-led growth with network expansion; resilient and defensive financial profile; execution-focused and disciplined management; and an "Asset-Light, Cash-Generating Model" where "Mature networks post initial build-out require moderating capex, generating stable free cash flow and improving ROCE".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Investor relations outsourced] Investor Relations contacts are listed at EY (arpit.mundra@in.ey.com, krishna.patel2@in.ey.com) alongside Director (Finance) Ashish Maheshwari and CFO Arun Kumar Saluru.
- [Standalone vs consolidated] The deck presents two near-identical P&L tables; the Q1FY27 headline PAT of Rs.34 crore is the standalone figure (34.32), while the consolidated table shows 33.81, and FY26 PAT differs at 56.89 (standalone) versus 53.20 (consolidated).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- **APM allocation CUT in Q4** + ceiling price $6.75→$7.00/MMBTU; NWG formula prices up — the core cost pressure. Fully passed through to CNG/industrial/commercial customers from April; "margins intact."
- HPHT price decline ($9.72→$8.92) and ~75-80% domestic sourcing for CNG cushion the cost. CGD enjoys priority-sector gas allocation, so domestic/mobility largely insulated vs industrial/power/fertilizer.
- **EV competition:** mgmt downplays — EV penetration "negligible" across GAs; only "some extent" a threat in Tamil Nadu (N&T). 3-wheeler EV conversion is "a debate." CNG vehicle additions still growing per Vahan data.
- Cost levers: type-3 cascades (~35% of fleet) and online stations to cut OpEx/scm; license fee 2% of net revenue; OpEx/scm to fall as volumes rise.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost (APM cut → high-cost gas; EV)

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** FY26 — Rev INR 1,066.66 cr (+9%), EBITDA INR 112.25 cr (+17%), PAT INR 56.89 cr (+21%), Volume 223.67 MMSCM (+9%), Net cash +INR 170 cr, 150 CNG stations (+39). Q4 PAT ~INR 13 cr (vs Q3 ~INR 15 cr) hit by 2 one-offs (INR 1.34 cr JV provision + INR 2.86 cr bank charge, both reversing Q1 FY27). APM allocation cut + ceiling $6.75→$7.00; NWG up; HPHT down $9.72→$8.92. FY27 guide: volume >250 MMSCM (double-digit / 30%+ on segments), EBITDA/scm INR 5.3-5.5, ~36 station adds, N&T capex INR 150-180 cr.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Volume growth FY27:** double-digit, "fairly 30% plus expectation" on segments; absolute volume to cross **250 MMSCM (maybe much more)** vs 223.67 in FY26. Per-segment growth: CNG / PNG-commercial / PNG-industrial each "more than 20% YoY"; industrial to catch up to 23-24% if NGT order implemented.
- **EBITDA/scm:** target **INR 5.3–5.5/scm** (from >INR 5.0); +10-15% improvement guided. Gross margin held at 25-26%.
- **Capex FY27:** Namakkal & Trichy alone INR 150 cr (internal target INR 170-180 cr). Funded by IPO funds (INR 194 cr available at Mar-end) for N&T; other 3 GAs via internal accruals + INR 40-45 cr term-loan line.
- **CNG station adds FY27:** ~36 new stations (vs 39 added in FY26).
- **Peak debt:** INR 70-80 cr range for FY27 (term loans ~INR 49 cr at Mar-end + INR 45 cr sanctioned).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- FY26 total volume 223.67 MMSCM (+9%). GA split (mgmt, volume basis): Banaskantha ~47%, Fatehgarh Sahib ~39%, balance DGS + Namakkal-Trichy.
- Pipeline network 6,695 inch-km. PNG connections: 83,262 domestic adds, 496 commercial, 223 industrial across 4 GAs in FY26.
- Banaskantha: 63,588 metered residential, 300+ commercial, 15+ industrial, 65 CNG stations. DGS crossed 10,000 domestic PNG. Namakkal-Trichy: 49 CNG stations, daily CNG demand ~doubled (100% jump) YoY.
outlook.title: Volume / pipeline

outlook.body:
- **New GA ramp:** Namakkal & Trichy is the flagship growth GA — INR 257 cr gross block to date, +INR 150-180 cr FY27 capex; 4-5 national/state highways pass through (mobility potential). MoU with TNSTC for PNG/CNG buses (71 running, +50 in May, ~6,000 kg/day, 17% of N&T CNG volume); Red Taxi Trichy MoU (120+ taxis converted); Trichy bus-stand CNG station planned.
- **LNG/LCNG:** first LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram (N&T); agreement with Ultra Gas Trading; lining up transporter hubs.
- **CBG/biogas:** tripartite IRM-GAIL-CBG-producer agreements across all 4 GAs under GAIL CBG-CGD Synchronization Scheme; Farm Gas (33% JV) supplying CBG from Khanna plant — "very profitable currently" amid gas shortage.
- **Backward integration:** Venuka Polymers (50% JV) — MDP P80/P100 pipes + irrigation + power-conduit; turnover expected to ~double / 2.5x next year.
- **Other:** Grasim Industries (DGS) & District Jail (BK) PNG MoUs for residential colonies; GreenMile+ fleet cards (Zaggle partnership).
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

deepdive.thesis: IRM is a fast-growing late-licensed (2017-19 era) CGD player across 4 GAs / 6 districts — Banaskantha (Gujarat, CNG-centric, ~49% of revenue), Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab, industrial-PNG heavy, ~36% of revenue), Diu & Gir-Somnath (DGS), and Namakkal & Trichy (Tamil Nadu, "aspirational" high-growth CNG GA). FY26 delivered 9% YoY volume and revenue growth with 17% EBITDA growth on a debt-light (net cash) balance sheet. The structural story is multi-decadal LPG→gas substitution with CNG (most profitable segment, ~61% of revenue) as the volume engine. Near-term overhang: geopolitical gas-sourcing disruption (Gulf war), APM allocation/ceiling-price pressure, and industrial demand softness in Fatehgarh Sahib. Mgmt insists margins are being protected via full cost pass-through.
